title_original: Junni Chen appointed inaugural director of Cheng-Lan Foundation
excerpt_original: Chen comes from Para Site, where she is currently deputy director

blocks.caption: Junni Chen. Photo: Ray Leung. Courtesy Cheng-Lan Foundation

blocks.text: Para Site’s Junni Chen has been appointed as the inaugural director and chief curator of Cheng-Lan Foundation in Hong Kong.

A graduate of Bard College’s Center of Curatorial Studies programme, Chen is currently deputy director of Para Site, a role she has served since 2024. Before that she was director at Tina Kim Gallery.

Chen’s appointment follows the launch of the foundation’s exhibition space Cheng-Lan Corner this March. At Cheng-Lan Foundation Chen will oversee its overall strategy and a public engagement programme featuring residencies, exhibitions and institutional collaborations with London’s Barbican and Delfina Foundation and Hong Kong’s Para Site.

Cheng-Lan Foundation was established in 2024 by collectors Brian Yue and Claire Bi Yu and named after the former’s grandmother. Exploring family and collective history of migration to Hong Kong, it started as a scholarship supporting artists of global majority and diaspora backgrounds.

In 2027, the Cheng-Lan Corner will present solo exhibitions by Shiraz Bayjoo and Cheong See Min. In London, the foundation will be supporting the Barbican Sculpture Court commission by Ximena Garrido-Lecca alongside an eight-week residency at Delfina Foundation.
